Wolf fell, and his stall was burning. The cattle came forth out of it, and the two brothers drove them to the pasture. Whoever breaks a pledge, Perkʷunos strikes him.

The cattle of Sky were in the earth, and a serpent guarded the door. The god came to the door and cried out: "Serpent, I am your friend. I bring you many sheep." A javelin wounded the Good One. The Good One fell from the chariot and lay upon the earth. His brother arrived and lifted him with his hands. The Good One spoke: "Brother, death has arrived for me. Lead my horses to the mother and say to her: 'Your son did not tremble before death.'" Then he died. The brother transported him by chariot to the mother. She caught sight of him and cried aloud, and her tears were flowing: "Beloved son, you lie upon the earth. You will not see the dawn, and you will not drive the swift horses. But your fame will not vanish." Then they laid him upon the fire, and the brother spoke to Fire: "Fire, carry my brother to the gods!" Then the fire burned him. Men remember his imperishable fame.
